decisive_items: Each episode featured subjective perioral swelling, hypotension within her baseline range, and stridor that resolved without objective edema
Direct laryngoscopy during one episode showed no airway edema or paradoxical vocal cord motion
Serial serum tryptase levels during acute events remained normal
response.rationale: Recurrent anaphylaxis-like episodes with only subjective swelling, normal laryngoscopy, normal tryptase, and no objective mediator or airway findings—combined with psychiatric comorbidity and an eating-disorder program—favor factitious disorder imposed on self over organic mast-cell, allergic, or angioedema causes.

rejected.why: No evidence that a caregiver is fabricating or producing the illness; the patient’s own reported symptoms and behaviors are central.
Normal serial tryptase, equivocal bone marrow findings, and absence of objective mast-cell mediator elevation argue against mastocytosis.
Initial symptoms mimicked anaphylaxis, but recurrent episodes lacked objective findings and had normal tryptase and laryngoscopy, making induced anaphylaxis unlikely.
Somatoform symptoms are generally unintentional; the subjective, inconsistent objective findings and repeated treatment-seeking suggest intentional symptom production.
Inducible mast cell activation syndrome is not supported by normal tryptase, unremarkable mediator workup, and no objective findings during episodes.
Hereditary angioedema was ruled out by normal testing, absence of edema on laryngoscopy, and episodes resolving without objective angioedema.
